verse.reading: Like a deer that takes a mirage for water and goes after it, fools see the life of this earth and rejoice; those who have seen the higher state do not talk empty bluster, but seek the feet of the True One; dance.
verse.nuance: The mirage-deer (கானல்மான்) closes the section on possessions by naming the error: not that wealth is bad but that it is not what it seems. மேனிலை கண்டார், those who have seen the higher state, are set against the வீம்பு (vaunting) of the world, which sits uneasily with the Siddhar's own boasts in 2005 to 2013.

finding.claim: Artemisinin, isolated from sweet wormwood after a search of traditional Chinese recipes, became a frontline malaria drug, showing traditional texts can point to real compounds.

verse.reading: We will turn the three worlds that cannot be described into red gold, make the hot sun's rays cool, and make this great world not exist; see our power and dance.
verse.nuance: Turning the worlds to gold extends the alchemist's transmutation to the cosmos; making the world not exist is read traditionally as the jnani's dissolving of the world in the void, as well as a feat of illusion.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: After that hear the five letters of Yamalai; when the five initiations are finished in due form, set yourself to the yoga called vaasi, son, and pranayama is completed; knowing all this, there is no obstacle, none, to the siddhi of the body; what is the world the Siddhars spoke of, best of men: it takes up again what was left unfinished, see.
verse.nuance: The order is mantra and initiation first, breath second, and the body-siddhi (காயசித்தி, the deathless body) as the fruit. விட்டகுறை எடுக்கும், taking up what was left off, is usually said of practice resumed from a former birth; here it may mean the Siddhars' world completes what one left undone. Yamalai has six letters in 1609 and five here, which may be two mantras or a slip.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: Are there firm gains without toil, or helplessness that does not come from failing to toil? So dig the stump of deceit root and all out of the field of the heart, clear it, lay out the bed called love, spread the manure called truth, plant the single seed of doubtless devotion, water it daily with the clear water of ardour, and fearing the five cattle that break in past every guard, go in and build the fence of peace; then the great sprout of knowledge rises, shows the tender shoot of compassion, the weeds of lust and anger are pulled, it grows straight, the hair bristles, tears bud, the fragrant flower opens and the rare fruit of the five letters appears, with poison throat, three eyes, eight shoulders, five bright faces, coral colour and white ash, sweeter than the six tastes, a joy to see, hear and think of; the ruby fruit of high Marudur ripens slowly into the hand, and our kind eat it and hold their heads high. Some do not come this way: they make the field of the mind a waste, let the forest of lust cover it where the hunters of the five senses rob, chase the mirage-chariot of pleasure that is never reached, the deer of untaught sense wanders, and when the seed of desire is dropped the great poison tree called 'I' shoots up, puts out branches of lies, spreads leaves of sin, buds cruelty, flowers harshness, hangs fruit of sorrow, ripens death and falls into the serpent's place: useless to themselves and others, they pass in the blink of an eye; such is their nature.
verse.nuance: The allegory is worked out stage by stage on both sides, cultivation and neglect, and the two trees are the Lord (the five-letter fruit wearing his own iconography) and the ego (யான் எனப் பெயரிய நச்சு மாமரம், the poison tree named 'I'). The five cattle and the five hunters are the senses in both halves. நாகிடை வீழ்ந்து, falling among the serpent, probably means hell; a variant reading is not recorded.

finding.claim: Case reports document severe poisoning, including cerebral edema, from Siddha capsules containing arsenic, mercury and lead thousands of times above safe limits.

verse.reading: As the sun and moon in the sky grew and then became one, the poet says he does not know the breathing of life within the fleshly body.
verse.nuance: கதிர் மதி, sun and moon, are the two breaths in Siddhar cipher, and their growing and becoming one is their joining in the middle channel, as tradition reads; the plain reading, that the sky's two lights become one (at new moon, or in eclipse), gives the simile its surface. உயிர்ப்பு is the breathing itself, the one practice the whole litany names directly.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

tamil: ஒழிந்த கருத்தினை வைத்து உள் எலும்பு வெள் எலும்பாய்க்
கழிந்த பிணம் போல் இருந்து காண்பது இனி எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will I keep the thought that has ceased, lie like a discarded corpse with the inner bone turned white bone, and see?
verse.nuance: ஒழிந்த கருத்து is thought that has stopped, or the one thought that remains when the rest have gone; the near-double at 23 has ஒழிந்த தருமம் instead. வெள் எலும்பு, the bone bleached white, is the corpse long dead; the poet asks to lie as one while still seeing (காண்பது), the living death of 89 and 139.

finding.claim: Reminders of death reliably shift people's attitudes and defence of their worldviews, a moderately sized effect across many studies, though recent large replications have been weaker.

verse.reading: A mother says that in this girl the sly glance has not appeared, the words are not understood, the hair has not reached the crest, the breasts have not budded and the gem-waist has not widened, that nothing has yet come to her in the land, and yet her heart has gone to the beautiful Ekambar.
verse.nuance: The repeated உற்றில (has not reached) lists the signs of womanhood that are missing, so the love is set before its season; the last line, உள்ளம் நல்கிடத்தே, may be 'in the giving of her heart' or 'as he gives her his heart'. I take it as the mother's wonder at a child's devotion.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: There is a fort with nine gates; inside it the keepers of the post are five; with love, the attendants are six; it is contained there, Maiden.
verse.nuance: The nine gates are the body's openings, a stock figure; the five keepers are the senses or the elements, and the six attendants (பரிகாரர்) the six adharas or the six faculties, as tradition takes them. The stanza's point is that the fort is guarded from within.

finding.claim: Elemental, inorganic and organic mercury are toxic to the nervous system and kidneys, and no safe therapeutic role for ingested mercury is established.

verse.reading: When will I leave the two country legs, go through the middle leg, and sit within the two goat legs?
verse.nuance: Wholly in cipher. நாட்டுக்கால் (the two legs planted in the country), நடுவுக்கால் (the middle leg) and ஆட்டுக்கால் (the two goat legs) are read by the tradition as ida and pingala, the sushumna, and a pair at the upper end (the two brows or two eyes, the 'moving' pair); 96 says the first two plainly. The plain words give a man stepping between legs of unlike kinds, which is not a sentence, so the cipher is the only reading.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: He takes body, wealth and life with the water of gift and changes the deeds of the gross body, the leveller; and (2205) he is the vision ida and pingala cannot reach.
verse.nuance: உதகத்தால் கொண்டு, taking with water, is the ritual of giving (the water poured over a gift), so the disciple makes a formal gift of self to the guru, and the guru in return alters the karma. சமனன் may be the impartial one or a form of சமன், Yama, who takes life; the first fits the context.

finding.claim: A single 25 mg dose of psilocybin with psychological support reduced treatment-resistant depression scores at three weeks more than 1 mg, with adverse events in both arms.

verse.reading: Not able to know the nature of the ida and pingala channels, the poet says he hesitated with obstruction.
verse.nuance: இடை and பிங்கலை are the left and right channels, sun and moon in the Siddhar cipher; இயல்பு, their nature, is their alternation, which the Tirumanthiram's வாரசரம் chapter teaches. தடை, obstruction, and தயங்கினேன், hesitated, describe a breath that would not move: the loss is in the practice itself.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: What is it that stands settled as the first of the five letters? What is it you chant, standing in the letter of the heart? What is it that the sword of the five letters cuts? You must separate out and tell the straight truth of the unripe letter.
verse.nuance: Three questions on the mantra's inside: its first (ஆதி), its place (நெஞ்சு), its work (அறுப்பு, cutting, as a sword). பிஞ்செழுத்து, the unripe or budding letter, is obscure, perhaps the seed-syllable or the letter before it is sounded; 1142's flower without a bud may be its pair.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: It is done: all the diseases in the body fly away when an atom of it is eaten; body-siddhi has grown great and one can live joined to the substance; take the oil of the thalaippindam, of the creeper and of the mango; after taking the oil add camphor without hesitation and do pooja to the substance with joy.
verse.nuance: தலைப்பிண்டம் is unexplained (a plant? a prepared ball?); கொடியும் மாவும் may be plant names or a powder. வத்து, the substance, is worshipped, the alchemical product treated as the god, which 2401 continues.

finding.claim: Artemisinin, isolated from sweet wormwood after a search of traditional Chinese recipes, became a frontline malaria drug, showing traditional texts can point to real compounds.

verse.reading: Because the dross of the salt changed as it oozed, before old age turns it to calx; by the salt this body hardens for crores of aeons, and in the vaasi that leaps at a word, the body.
verse.nuance: சுன்னம் (calx, the calcined ash) is an alchemical end-product and here what old age makes of the body; the salt properly treated is claimed to keep the body for கற்பாந்தம் கோடி, crores of kalpas. The last line brings in வாசி, the breath practice, so the hardened body is kept by breath as well as by salt; the syntax is broken and the reading is a reconstruction.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: All that is cause, demon, I have told as I saw it; you have seen the destruction too, and all the ways in which they came.
verse.nuance: காரணம் gathers the causes listed so far. மாரணம் is killing or destruction (in tantric lists one of the six rites); here it most likely means that everything that came also perishes.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: A house eight spans long, and in it a filth-nest of eight and one; the panchayat men are twice five, and they said this is the city of god, jnana girl.
verse.nuance: The eight-span body is standard. எட்டொரு பீற்றன் மலக்கூடு is obscure: 'the nine-fold nest of filth' (the nine openings) or 'a filth-nest of eight tatters'. The ten who declare it god's city are read as the ten airs or the ten senses, and the stanza turns on their being right despite the filth.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: Just be still, demon; I have told you the formula. The place where you stayed still is what was pointed to.
verse.nuance: சும்மா இரு (simply be, do nothing) is the work's one positive instruction, called a சூத்திரம் in mockery of the sutras rejected in 1674. சுட்டது is from சுட்டு (to point out) or சுடு (to burn); the stillness is either the thing indicated or the thing that burns away the rest. 1686 and 1690 repeat it.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: The thought takes the body, a bubble on water, for permanent; the desire that rises above all says 'I will not perish'.
verse.nuance: நீர்க்குமிழி, the water bubble, is the Naladiyar's image for the body (27). ஆர்க்கும் உயர் ஆசை may be the desire higher than all others or the desire that rises in everyone; it closes the run of speaking desires.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: Milk the milk that does not go bad; milk so as to live on day after day; milk the milk that flows without ceasing; milk the milk that grows in the skull.
verse.nuance: தலை மண்டை, the skull, names the source directly; the three qualities (not stinking, unceasing, giving long life) are the tradition's claims for the inner nectar against the body's milk, which sours.

finding.claim: Maximum human lifespan appears to have plateaued near 115-125 years, and radical life extension in this century is judged implausible.

verse.reading: If someone seeks out the place where I am and brings food for my hunger with eagerness, I will eat; even if they call me with much insistence I will not go, Hara; even if the body wastes away, from now on I will not go.
verse.nuance: A vow stricter than begging: the poet will not enter a house even when invited, and eats only what is carried to him. ஏகம் இளைத்தாலும், even if the body wastes, accepts starvation as the price, which 407 shows being paid.

finding.claim: Intermittent fasting improves metabolic markers in animals and some humans, but trials show weight loss similar to ordinary calorie restriction.

verse.reading: When will I cut and burn the dense forest of the mind, striking again and again with the sword that is the five letters?
verse.nuance: The mantra is a weapon against the mind rather than an offering to the Lord, and the cutting must be repeated (தொடர்ந்து தொடர்ந்து). The sword of letters returns at 117, where the letters va and ma become the blade.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: After you have sought and held within yourselves, for four nazhigai, the light that sprouted and rose in the root channel, you may live as a child and may become the supreme Brahman; by the oath of the one who ate the poison and by the Mother's oath, this is true.
verse.nuance: மூலநாடி is the channel at the root (the base of the spine), and the light that rises in it is what tradition calls kundalini, though the verse does not use the word. நாலு நாழி is four nazhigai, about ninety-six minutes, a daily measure of practice. The two results, a child's body and Brahman-hood, are given together, as at 968.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: In the beginning the sound born of the Supreme became Parasiva, formless-with-form; as the place of Siva called light it became Shakti; in the old world it became the sevenfold creation; standing as itself by the knowledge called order it became the full partless one; and by the grace of Shakti and Siva, Shanmuga and Ganapati came to be.
verse.nuance: Creation is traced from sound (சத்தம்), as in Tirumular's nada, and the two sons are the last and most concrete stage. எழுவகைத் தோற்றம் is the seven kinds of birth. சாதியென்ற is a rhyme-word whose sense here ('kind', 'gentle') is loose.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Is it the mass of coarse hair, or the stretch of skin the hair grows on, or the wound packed inside the skin, or the blood that wells in the wound, or the bones standing here and there between, or the stinking marrow that drips from the bones, or the slime that oozes within, or the orderly files of crawling worms, or the heap of excrement set in water, or the ropes of tied nerves, or the disease that never leaves the body: which of these is 'I', I do not know; I searched everywhere and found it nowhere. Then, Lord of Marudur who burnt the three cities with one mountain bow, made Kama fine dust with a glance, turned the fire-mouthed poison to nectar so the gods would not die, stood beyond the two who sought you, and scorched Death for the boy's sake, half-woman, lord of Ganga, Lord of the Kaveri-girt grove where nine gems shine without the sun: because your divine grace came into my hand, I tore the veil of maya and gained the pure eye of knowledge; and having gained it I saw your greatness, and seeing it I saw myself, and saw others, and saw myself in all your states; those who do not see you are the kind that do not see themselves.
verse.nuance: The dissection is a search for the self, each part posed as a question (ஓ), and the answer is that the self is not found in the body but given by grace along with the sight of the Lord. The order of seeing matters: the Lord first, then oneself, then others, then oneself in all his states. The variant தெரியாது இன்ன (not discerning, this) for தெரிதரல் இன்ன does not change the sense.

finding.claim: A model holds that psychedelics relax the brain's high-level prior beliefs, letting bottom-up signals revise entrenched self-models.

verse.reading: Is not the fit true learning the learning learned in order to be silent? Work it out, stony mind.
verse.nuance: Learning has silence as its end, not speech or debate; வாகான, fitting or well-formed, marks this as the true kind among the learnings of 1794.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: Beyond the four Vedas, hard for Narayana and the four-faced one who resolved to know him, the Full One who fills the middle, our father, the Lord of Pugali, the cause of every world, the core thing beyond the inner faculties.
verse.nuance: பூரணன் and கருப்பொருள் are the two names the verse adds to the usual list: the Lord is the Full One and the kernel beyond the antahkarana (mind, intellect, will, ego). Pattinathar uses பூரணம் as a name of the Lord here as throughout his Pooranamalai; the medical Siddhars make it a technical term.

finding.claim: Ageing reflects a set of interacting cellular hallmarks such as genomic instability, loss of protein balance and stem-cell exhaustion, none yet reversed in humans.

verse.reading: As the sun hides the shining stars, when will I see your sight, free of any stain?
verse.nuance: The stars are not put out but outshone; the Lord's appearing hides all else by its light, and களங்கமற may qualify the sight or the seer.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: One must win the boon of not being born; and having been born, there is a medicine for not dying, see how it is: heart, do not forget the lotus feet of the Lord of the dharma-rich hall of Tillai; see, that is the good medicine for you.
verse.nuance: இறவாதிருக்க மருந்து, a medicine against dying, is the Siddhars' promise, usually kept by breath or kalpa herbs; Pattinathar names remembrance of the feet as the drug. Whether the deathlessness is bodily or the end of rebirth is not said.

finding.claim: A single 25 mg dose of psilocybin with psychological support reduced treatment-resistant depression scores at three weeks more than 1 mg, with adverse events in both arms.

verse.reading: When will I stand contained within the letter a, with the letter va and the letter ma become the sword, and the letter si?
verse.nuance: The letters are those of சிவாயநம: va, ma and si are named, and அவ்வெழுத்து is the letter a (the first of Om, as the Kural's அகர முதல) or 'that letter'. The sword returns from 84: there the five letters together cut the mind, here two of them are the blade and the rest are sheathed in a. Tradition reads such letter-verses as the breath's syllables; the plain sense is the mantra folded into its first sound.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: Mounting the vaasi gently in the silent five letters, after entering the sphere of light that filled up to the sky; in the measure in which he and I mingled in truth and experienced it, he is and I am not, and it became 'no one'.
verse.nuance: வாசி ஏறி, riding the breath, is the Siddhars' word for breath-practice, and the mantra is its mount. The last line moves in three steps: he exists, I do not, no one at all; the verse does not stop at the first. மவுன அஞ்செழுத்து, the silent five letters, is the mantra said without sound.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: It flew, when it renounced, by the way of Paychalur; it forgot, settled in the hand of the warriors who seized it; it was born; at the moment of death, in the 'kī' without harm, the silence that excelled became clear: Sivayam.
verse.nuance: The formula of 1328 with the verbs changed: flew, forgot, was born, and at death the silence cleared. வாணர், the warriors or the Vanar, who seize may be the senses or Death's men; பீடிடாமல், without harm or without seat, is unclear. The pair of stanzas tells the breath's whole career from entry to exit.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: Giving up salt is desire, eating food only once a day is desire; join the Manonmani god who cannot be spoken and dance the kummi.
verse.nuance: The vows of abstaining from salt and of a single daily meal are reckoned with desire, as wanting a result. The salt here is literal, unlike the coded salt of 2648, so the kummi both praises knowing the salt and dismisses giving it up. மனோன்மணி is the Shakti of the crown, 'jewel of the mind'.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: Certain that this body, an unstable false cage, has no substance, the poet in fear went to a mountain cave, learned the way of Sivajnana and became straight in it.
verse.nuance: அச்சமதோடு: fear is the motive for retreat, an honest detail. The body contempt here sits against 2324, where the fleshly body is kept from perishing in nishtai; the song holds both without reconciling them.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: The desire to learn the arts says 'I will not leave off'; the desire to learn siddhis says 'I will not be broken'.
verse.nuance: The siddhis, the Siddhars' own goal, are named here as one more craving beside learning; the verse treats the wish for powers as a bond, not a path.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: Where Nandi sat is the fire-circle; the gaze fixed on the middle of the brows is the mark; the moon and the ray-sun stood in that place, jnana girl.
verse.nuance: The three lights of 2570 are now placed: fire where Nandi sits, sun and moon at the brow-centre where the gaze is held. In the cipher sun and moon are the two breaths, pingalai and idai, which meet at the brow; both the plain and the coded sense stand.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: You mutes who swing to and fro, pitying the whirling gate: you do not think of opening the whirling gate to reach the truth; after you open the whirling gate and perceive the truth, you yourselves become the truth that was inside the whirling gate.
verse.nuance: உழலும் வாசல் (the whirling or turning gate) repeats in every line; tradition takes it as the womb-gate that keeps one turning in births, and as the inner door of 1031. ஊசலாடும் (swinging) is the oscillation of the undecided mind. The last line is identity, not vision: the opener becomes what was behind the door.

finding.claim: Siddha polyherbal decoctions such as Nilavembu and Kaba Sura Kudineer have been tested in few, small COVID-19 trials, with uncertain benefit beyond standard care.

verse.reading: Young men whose minds rush to the corner of the spear-like dark eyes of the fine maidens, heedless of the cruelty of the leaping bulls, hold them in Kambar's Kanchi; and in the fields of young jasmine fed by sluices, as fawns and calves bound through every gate, the village green fills and surges like a sea.
verse.nuance: The desire that drives the youths at the bulls is said straight: it is the maidens' eyes, not valour. The sea simile that opened the chapter (929) returns for the crowd on the green.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: He of unchanging fame and the honey garland, the Siva-yogi of silence who does not open his mouth to rage; and straight (2197) his guru is Chitrambalavan.
verse.nuance: வாய்திறந்து சீறாத: silence is defined as not opening the mouth in anger, a narrower and more practical mounam than the stilling of all thought. Yet 2194 gave him fury; the anger is turned on the disciples' enemies, not spoken.

finding.claim: Curcumin, though popular, is unstable, poorly absorbed and a frequent false positive in assays, and no double-blind trial has shown a clear therapeutic benefit.

verse.reading: Returning from the letter 'ming' with 'kū', sleeping with the moon, the moon changes and stands; because in the whirl of the body's great point it becomes one, darkness ends, meditation is complete, and the flame-light is seen.
verse.nuance: அங்கமா முனைச்சுழி, the whirl at the body's great point, is the central channel's opening at the brow or crown as tradition reads it; the moon changing is the breath moving from one channel to the other. மிங்கு and கியானம் (for ஞானம்) look like dialect or copying errors. கங்குலற்று, darkness gone, is the one plain phrase.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: They say the flying mercury is done, they say they have made even the needle-magnet into a cup; it is by the trickery of their world-alchemy that they make a living, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: கவன சூதம், mercury fixed so that it gives the power to fly (கமனம்), and the magnet worked into a vessel are boasts of the alchemical literature. புவனவாதை may be புவன வாதம், alchemy for the world's eyes, against the inner alchemy the kummi prefers.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.
